Hi Sarah / MedCare procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — the discovery call was really helpful for understanding your use case (clinical notes ingestion + summarization for provider workflows). Per our conversation, I wanted to recap the security/compliance items you asked about and outline next steps so we all have the same expectations.

Summary of ask:
- Confirm whether Redwood can support PHI (BAA) and which deployment modes are eligible.
- Share SOC 2 report and BAA template.
- Kick off vendor security questionnaire (we can own the majority and loop in security for any deep technical items).

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployment modes (VPC / on-prem). Our hosted public API is not approved for storing/processing PHI by default.
- PHI boundaries: we recommend Dedicated or Private if you will send PHI. Those modes support customer-managed KMS, audit logging, and optional no-persistent-logs configuration.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll attach our standard BAA template and the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (see attachments).
2) If that looks good, Procurement can return a redline to me and I will loop legal (cc'd: Rishi) — we typically turn around BAA redlines within 7–10 business days.
3) We'll start the vendor security questionnaire once procurement confirms scope; our security lead (Monica) will join the kickoff for any technical deep-dives.

Can you confirm whether MedCare will be sending PHI in initial integration (pilot) or if you'll start with de-identified / tokenized data? That determines whether we need Dedicated/Private for the pilot.

Thanks — attaching the BAA and SOC 2 now.

Best,

Sarah — thanks for the detailed questions. Answers below and next steps.

1) Hosted API and PHI:
- The public hosted API endpoint is not approved for PHI / BAA-covered data. We can make contractual commitments for Dedicated and Private deployments only.
- There is no supported hosted configuration that effectively makes the public endpoint BAA-eligible; for customers needing PHI we recommend Dedicated (tenant-isolated GPU pools) or Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem).

2) Retention & KMS:
- Default: Redwood retains request/response logs for 30 days for operational debugging; logs can be turned off for PHI scoped workloads on Dedicated/Private.
- KMS: Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS (you can provide keys via AWS KMS or supported HSM).
- Audit logs: Dedicated/Private provide full per-request audit logs and can be forwarded to your logging endpoint.

3) BAA & SOC2:
- I'm attaching our standard BAA template and the SOC 2 Type II report we shared. We do sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private customers.

4) Deployment ETA and cost band (pilot):
- ETA: Dedicated capacity for a small pilot can typically be provisioned in 2–4 weeks after contract signature and initial deposit. Private on-prem timelines vary (4–8 weeks).
- Cost band: ballpark monthly ranges for a pilot: Dedicated (small) ~$25k–$40k/month depending on throughput; Private (on-prem) variable (involves licensing + infra). We'll provide a formal quote once we scope throughput and SLAs.

5) Security questionnaire & kickoff:
- Monica will handle the security questionnaire. Monica, can you take the first pass on answers and propose a 30-minute time window for a kickoff this week or early next?

Next steps (proposed):
- Sarah/Procurement: review the attached BAA and redline if needed.
- Redwood: Monica to complete vendor questionnaire initial pass; Marissa/Rishi to coordinate BAA redlines and contract.
- Schedule a pilot scoping call to finalize throughput and ETA.

If helpful, I can send a short mutual action plan doc after we align on next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
